feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy/operations leadership. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, tighter section consolidation, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within the same organization strongly signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Good scope and relevance: combines strategy, web/CMS, analytics, governance, and multimedia in a way that fits modern digital communications leadership roles.  
- Generally strong writing: concise, professional, and easy to follow, with no major spelling errors or obvious typos.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include measurable impact where possible (engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, adoption, cost savings, campaign results).  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: use “12+ years of experience” instead of “more than 12 years experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); consider consistent date formatting (“Sept.”/“Oct.”) and title casing (e.g., “Topline Skills”).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be stronger with sharper positioning, one or two concrete signals of scale, and slightly less overlap with the skills sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Lead with your current value proposition: senior digital strategy/communications leadership for mission-driven or advocacy-focused organizations.
- Add one concrete scale marker from recent roles, such as leading a 10,000+ page Drupal migration or overseeing channels reaching tens of thousands.
- Trim broad skill lists (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) since these are already covered elsewhere; emphasize outcomes and specialization instead.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience building and modernizing cross-channel programs for mission-driven organizations. Combines editorial leadership, platform modernization, and workflow design to improve how teams publish, coordinate, and measure digital communications. Brings deep experience in advocacy messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. It would be sharper if grouped around higher-value capabilities and phrased more distinctly.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and modernize wording: “Multi-channel communications,” “Web platform administration,” and “Editorial systems design” read more polished and consistent.
- Emphasize senior-level strengths over generic tasks; for example, foreground strategy, governance, platform modernization, analytics, and advocacy communications.
- Consider a more differentiated version: Digital strategy & platform modernization • Editorial systems & governance • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS administration • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Keep style consistent: use either all singular or all plural nouns where possible.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header summary.
- “Workflow & systems architecture” and “Editorial workflow design” are close enough that they may feel repetitive.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a service list. Tighten around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or deliverables to distinguish it from your NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets on systems/workflows/governance into one impact-focused line: “Built digital workflows, analytics, and governance practices that improved coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Make Drupal/CMS work more outcome-led: “Designed and launched Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.” Add metrics if possible: number of sites, users, publishers, or turnaround gains.
- Keep the AI search bullet, but make it more distinctive: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content architecture, and user-facing discovery experiences for complex policy/member content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance/usability/operational best practices” overlaps with prior NACo governance bullets; keep only if tied to a new result.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may duplicate skills sections unless linked to a notable launch or scale.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles. Lead with transformation, systems, and measurable scope.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, budget, and multi-channel communications operations.”
- Combine and tighten web impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page site to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes explicit where possible: add budget size, team size, reporting improvements, production volume, engagement growth, or efficiency gains from governance/analytics.
- Rephrase weaker bullets to show business value: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring video series.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; either add distinct results here or cut it.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo entries unless this bullet stresses the studio build and organizational scale-up.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like responsibilities than achievements. Tighten it to emphasize scope, channel ownership, and systems/process impact distinct from the later director role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging organization-wide.”
- Combine newsletter/video bullets and make outcomes clearer: “Owned four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders, and produced a weekly advocacy video series that established video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Recast coordination/process bullets into stronger action language: “Built cross-team editorial planning routines linking communications, advocacy and program staff, improving alignment, publishing consistency and campaign execution.”
- If possible, add metrics: open rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or number of teams/stakeholders supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager role and footer project; distinguish this role as scaling/formalizing the series.
- “Improved workflows” overlaps with the Director role’s governance language; focus here on operational coordination rather than enterprise standards.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent experience. It should be tightened to emphasize senior-level scope and distinct strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, leadership-level wording tied to enterprise environments.
- Reduce overlap with “Core Competencies” by focusing on strategy/governance rather than repeating channel operations.
- Suggested rewrite:
- Enterprise digital strategy and modernization
- Editorial governance and content operating models
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy and planning

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” closely duplicate both the header and Core Competencies.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with work experience bullets on web, email, social, and video leadership; avoid repeating channel lists here.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. Tighten it into a sharper topline summary that emphasizes current, higher-value capabilities over listing every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Prioritize most relevant/recent strengths first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations/automation.
- Remove lower-signal items if space is tight; consider dropping WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages from this topline and leaving them in “Technical + IT.”
- Use parallel phrasing and fewer bullets/terms to improve scanability; “technical execution” should imply delivery, not just platform familiarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies and the header summary; keep it here only if it remains a priority differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for a senior digital leader, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. This topline version should emphasize strategic application and decision-making, not just platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led wording, e.g. “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization” rather than a software list.
- Tighten and group items: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity” + “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider adding one higher-value phrase tied to recent work, such as “analytics infrastructure” or “decision-ready dashboards,” to align with the NACo director role.
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio & Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding and leadership reporting • SEO, UX and performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates the “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section in Technical + IT almost exactly.
- “Leadership reporting” may be better phrased as “executive reporting” for sharper senior-level positioning.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value production leadership and event delivery rather than generic tools.

Suggested edit:

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Use it to signal depth and recency—especially Drupal—rather than repeat a raw tool list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a flat list to a capability-led line, e.g.: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Put the strongest/recent platform first and consider adding level cues: **Drupal (advanced)** if accurate, since recent roles and projects are Drupal-heavy.
- If space allows, tie one platform to scale or context: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; 3.5M annual page views)**.
- Consider dropping the title “CMS” from the content itself and keeping only platforms here; save implementation detail for the coding/technical line.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution” entry almost exactly; differentiate or remove one.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel lightweight versus enterprise platforms unless supported elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation-level tools and modernize the phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/reshape as: **Front-End & Technical Implementation:** HTML/CSS • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers unless required: use **HTML/CSS** instead of **HTML5/CSS3** for cleaner, less dated wording.
- Consider removing **jQuery** or moving it to the end as “legacy support,” unless it is still central in recent work.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work: **front-end implementation, tagging, serverless scripting, and deployment automation**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution** (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations”). Keep one broad, one implementation-specific.
- **GitHub Actions** may also overlap conceptually with “Workflow automation”; keep it here only if framed as deployment/CI rather than general automation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere. Make it more purposeful by grouping tools by function and emphasizing systems/automation over basic collaboration apps.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Systems**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If accurate, add light qualifiers instead of a bare list: **Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate/Zapier (process automation) • Jira/Asana/Trello (project workflows) • Slack/Teams/Basecamp (team coordination)**
- Consider trimming lower-value/general tools if space is tight; keep the platforms most tied to operational systems and automation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools; listing both may add less value than highlighting automation-specific platforms.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare relative to the rest of the CV. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should stay tool-focused and avoid restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of generic tools: **enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- If space allows, make it slightly more outcome-oriented via category wording, e.g. **Email Marketing, Automation & Community Platforms:** Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “audience growth,” or “tens of thousands reached” here; that impact is already covered well in the NACo experience entries.
- Don’t repeat “multi-channel communications” language already captured in Core Competencies and recent roles.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this reads broadly and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs if you can quantify them.

Suggested edit
- Reframe around early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted through two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Tighten phrasing and reduce channel list repetition: “improved publishing workflows across web, email, social and video” instead of “strengthening workflows…”
- Add measurable scope where possible: website refresh size, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience/reach, or team size supported.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted through two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving publishing workflows across web, email, social and video. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly advocacy video updates, while providing day-to-day guidance to a junior digital staff member.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; distinguish this as launching/producing the series rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already used more strongly in later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a notable “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize innovation/program support and the podcast launch as the standout result.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy work; partnered with internal teams to translate findings into digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the podcast line sharper and outcome-oriented: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Cut generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production”; specify deliverables if possible (e.g., briefs, web features, multimedia assets).
- If you have metrics, add one: number of episodes launched, audience growth, stakeholder groups served, or projects supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later NACo roles; keep this entry focused on research/innovation coordination plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid overemphasizing video/multimedia here since later roles show much stronger, more recent leadership in that area.
